findings: DETERMINISTIC + SAFE to share: pure recipes (export-default or bare-body-using-ctx.input) with no Math.random/Date/time/IO.
BREAKS: bare function body referencing bare `input` (must be ctx.input, or use export-default which gets (input,ctx)). This is the E3 gotcha as a class — an input-contract mismatch.

NON-DETERMINISTIC: Math.random is a clear failure (different output every run). Time (Date.now/new Date) is also non-deterministic in reality; my 2-back-to-back-runs probe gave a FALSE PASS because both ran in the same millisecond — the test is too tight to catch time nondeterminism. Honest: do NOT conclude time-recipes are deterministic; the probe just didn't separate the calls.
limitation: The probe ran each shape twice back-to-back. That catches Math.random but NOT sub-ms time variance. A stronger E5b would space runs or inject a clock to prove time-dependence.
implication: Sharing safety = a recipe is safe to share/compose iff it is pure (no random/time/IO) AND uses the correct input contract. pantry could lint/flag these at push time (follow-on).
